mainTopic: The length of the הפטרה, the rituals that need a מנין of ten and their sources, and the minimum Torah reading
overview: This amud first finishes the discussion of how long the הפטרה must be. The basic rule is 21 פסוקים, though רבא points out a shorter הפטרה that is still read. The גמרא allows fewer פסוקים when the topic ends, or when a תורגמן is translating. A new משנה then lists the public rituals that need ten men: ברכות before שמע, חזרת הש"ץ, ברכת כהנים, קריאת התורה, הפטרה, funeral and wedding blessings, and זימון with הקב"ה's name. The גמרא learns that every דבר שבקדושה needs ten from ״ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל״, through a chain of גזירות שוות ending with the ten מרגלים. Other items need ten only out of respect. Valuing consecrated land or a person takes nine ישראלים and one כהן. שמואל derives this from the ten mentions of כהן, and his derivation ends with an unanswered קשיא. The amud closes with a new משנה: each reader reads at least three פסוקים, and gives the מתורגמן only one פסוק at a time.

steps.title: No extra הפטרה verses are needed for the מפטיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the מפטיר's own Torah reading does not add three more פסוקים to the הפטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Since the מפטיר's Torah reading is only for the honor of the תורה,] it is also not necessary to read verses corresponding to him.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that began on the previous amud. It explains why the מפטיר, who is also called to the תורה, does not raise the הפטרה from 21 to 24 פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 21 פסוקים equal seven readers times three פסוקים each. The מפטיר is an extra, eighth reader, so one might think he adds three more פסוקים. The answer is that his Torah reading is extra, done for כבוד התורה, so it does not count toward the total.

keyTerms.meaning: corresponding to him (matching his reading)
also
is not needed
the person who reads the הפטרה from the נביא

phrases.english: corresponding to him also is not necessary.
phrases.notes: The end of the answer about the מפטיר. His Torah reading is for honor only, so no extra הפטרה פסוקים are needed for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer earlier about counting the מפטיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the מפטיר's reading is extra and does not count toward the seven
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מפטיר is an eighth reader, so the הפטרה should be 24 פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: His reading is for כבוד התורה only, so the count stays at 21.

steps.title: רבא points to a הפטרה shorter than 21 verses
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the 21-פסוקים rule from the הפטרה of עולותיכם ספו, which is shorter and is still read.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: But there is the הפטרה beginning "Add your burnt offerings" (ירמיה ז), which does not have twenty-one פסוקים, and we read it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the rule that a הפטרה must be at least 21 פסוקים. He points to a real הפטרה that is shorter and is read anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 21 פסוקים were a strict minimum, the custom of reading עולותיכם ספו would break the rule. Either the rule is wrong, or there is an exception that still needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: he strongly objected to it
"Add your burnt offerings", the opening of a הפטרה from ירמיה
twenty-one
we read

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to it:
But there is "Add your burnt offerings,"
phrases.notes: ירמיה ז:כא–כח, the הפטרה for פרשת צו.

phrases.english: which are not twenty-one, and we read it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 21-פסוקים rule that the previous step assumed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a הפטרה must be at least 21 פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An accepted practice contradicts the rule: a shorter הפטרה is read.

steps.title: A shorter הפטרה is fine when the topic ends
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עולותיכם ספו is different because its topic comes to a close.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because the topic is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 21-פסוקים rule by limiting it. When the topic finishes in fewer פסוקים, there is no need to start a new topic just to reach 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 21 still stands in general. The exception is narrow: a completed topic is a good stopping point, and adding unrelated material would be worse than reading fewer פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: there it is different
finished, completed
the topic or subject matter

phrases.english: There it is different, since the topic is completed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule with an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 21 פסוקים is required always, so a shorter הפטרה should not be read.
steps.terutzMaskana: 21 פסוקים is the rule unless the topic ends sooner.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן stopped after ten verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: רבי יוחנן told the reader to stop after ten פסוקים, even when the topic had not ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where the topic is not completed, may one not stop? Didn't רב שמואל בר אבא say: Many times I stood before רבי יוחנן, and when we had read ten פסוקים, he would tell us: Stop!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the exception just given. It brings a report that רבי יוחנן had them stop after only ten פסוקים, with no mention of the topic ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer implied that a short הפטרה is allowed only when the topic finishes. רבי יוחנן's practice suggests stopping early is allowed even without that, so the exception seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't [so-and-so] say?
many times
I would stand before him
stop!

phrases.english: And where the topic is not completed, not?
But didn't Rav Shmuel bar Abba say:
Many times I would stand
before Rabbi Yochanan,
and when we had read ten verses,
he would say to us: Stop!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא דְּלָא סָלֵיק עִנְיָינָא לָא? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the exception from step 3 as being too narrow.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a shorter הפטרה is allowed only when the topic ends
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן stopped at ten פסוקים without any mention of the topic ending.

steps.title: A place with a translator is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's case had a תורגמן, and that allows stopping early.
steps.simpleTranslation: A place where there is a translator is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's practice with a second exception: when a תורגמן translates each פסוק, the reading can be shorter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Translating each פסוק, often with extra explanation, takes a long time. To avoid burdening the community (טורח הציבור), fewer פסוקים are enough. So there are now two exceptions: the topic ending, and the presence of a תורגמן.

keyTerms.meaning: translator who renders each פסוק into Aramaic for the community
place

phrases.english: A place where there is a translator is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יוחנן's practice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stopping after ten פסוקים contradicts the 21 rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: When there is a תורגמן, one may stop early.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the תורגמן exception
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא בר שמואל taught that the 21-פסוקים rule applies only where there is no תורגמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב תחליפא בר שמואל taught: They taught [21 פסוקים] only in a place where there is no translator, but in a place where there is a translator, one may stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a ברייתא. It states outright that the 21-פסוקים requirement is limited to places without a translator.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לא שנו אלא limits an earlier rule to a specific case. This turns the תורגמן answer from a guess into a source-based rule.

keyTerms.meaning: as [he] taught (introduces a ברייתא)
they taught this only in the case of
he stops

steps.whatToRemember: A הפטרה is normally 21 פסוקים, three for each of the seven Torah readers. You may read fewer if the topic ends, or if a תורגמן is translating.

phrases.english: As Rav Tachalifa bar Shmuel taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין תּוּרְגְּמָן,
phrases.english: They taught this only in a place where there is no translator,
but in a place where there is a translator, one may stop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source supporting the answer in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a תורגמן allows a shorter הפטרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב תחליפא בר שמואל

steps.title: New משנה: rituals that need a minyan
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing public rituals that may not be done with fewer than ten men.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One does not recite the introductory blessing before שמע, nor does one pass before the ark, nor do the כהנים lift their hands, nor is the תורה read, nor does one conclude with the נביא [with fewer than ten].
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It lists public rituals that need a מנין, and the words "with fewer than ten" come right later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is a public act of holiness: פורס על שמע, חזרת הש"ץ, ברכת כהנים, קריאת התורה, and הפטרה. The גמרא will later look for the source that these need ten.

keyTerms.meaning: leading the public blessings before קריאת שמע
passing before the ark, i.e. leading the עמידה as חזן
the כהנים lifting their hands for ברכת כהנים
reading the concluding portion from the נביאים

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "with fewer than ten" (פחות מעשרה) only comes at the end of the list, in step 8. Every "אין" here means "not with fewer than ten", not "never".

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One does not lead the blessing over Shema,
nor does one pass before the ark,
nor do they lift their hands,
nor do they read from the Torah,
nor do they conclude with the Prophets,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a new משנה about the requirement of ten men.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These public rituals may not be done without a מנין of ten.

steps.title: More rituals that need ten men
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. מעמד ומושב, ברכת אבלים, תנחומי אבלים, ברכת חתנים, and a זימון with הקב"ה's name all need ten men.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not do the 'standing and sitting' at a funeral. We do not say the mourners' blessing, comfort the mourners in a line, or say the חתן's blessings. And we do not lead a זימון with הקב"ה's name. None of these may be done with fewer than ten men.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing public rituals that need a מנין of ten. It ends this part of the list with the words 'fewer than ten.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new items are about mourning, weddings, and ברכת המזון. The words פחות מעשרה at the end apply to every item in the list, including the ones from step 7. In a זימון, saying הקב"ה's name ('נברך לאלקינו') is the part that needs ten.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'standing and sitting': a ceremony of stopping and sitting on the way back from a funeral
A blessing said for mourners
Comforting mourners, as people stand in rows after the burial
The wedding blessings (שבע ברכות)
Leading a זימון using הקב"ה's name (אלקינו)

steps.confusionAlert: A זימון itself only needs three people. Only the version that adds הקב"ה's name needs ten.

phrases.english: And we do not do the 'standing and sitting' (at a funeral),
and we do not say the mourners' blessing
or the comforting of mourners,
or the blessing of grooms,
and we do not lead a zimmun with (God's) name —
with fewer than ten.
phrases.notes: This closes the whole list that began in step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes the משנה's list from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעמד ומושב, ברכת אבלים, תנחומי אבלים, ברכת חתנים, and זימון בשם all need at least ten men.

steps.title: Valuing consecrated land or a person needs nine plus a priest
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that valuing consecrated land needs ten people, one of whom is a כהן. The same applies to valuing a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for land, the valuation is done by nine people and a כהן. A person is valued the same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case that needs ten. Here the ten must include a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is not about prayer. It is about הקדש: someone gave land to the בית המקדש and wants to buy it back, or someone pledged his own value. The court that sets the price has ten people, and one of them must be a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Land, here land that was given to הקדש
Nine people plus one כהן, ten in total
The same as them, following the same rule

phrases.english: And for (consecrated) land — nine and a priest,
and a person (being valued) is like them.
phrases.notes: This refers to someone who pledged his own value to the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last case to the משנה's list, and this one comes with an extra condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Valuing consecrated land, or a person, is done by ten: nine people and a כהן.

steps.title: Where do we learn the need for ten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the source that these things need ten men.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Where do we learn these things from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule of ten. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule but did not explain where it comes from. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows the number ten.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
'From where are these things?' A request for the source

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters (derived)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that these rituals need ten men.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: anything holy needs ten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings the פסוק ״ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל״. It teaches that any דבר שבקדושה needs at least ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The פסוק says, 'And I will be made holy among the children of Israel.' This teaches that anything holy may not be done with fewer than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It gives a פסוק and a general rule: holy matters need ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is ״ונקדשתי״, the מצוה to make הקב"ה's name holy in public. From it we get one rule that covers the list: any דבר שבקדושה needs ten. But the פסוק does not say the number ten, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And I will be made holy', from ויקרא כ"ב:ל"ב
A matter of holiness, like קדיש, קדושה, and ברכו
'For the פסוק says'

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'כל דבר שבקדושה needs ten' is the basic source for why we need a מנין for קדיש, קדושה, and ברכו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
For the verse says:
"And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel,"
any matter of holiness
may not be with fewer than ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ״ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל״: any דבר שבקדושה needs ten.

steps.title: How does the verse show the number ten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק ״ונקדשתי״ shows the number ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this come out of the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about רבי יוחנן's source. It is setting up רבי חייא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'among the children of Israel' but gives no number. So how do we know it means exactly ten?

keyTerms.meaning: 'How is this implied?' A request to show how the פסוק teaches the point

phrases.english: From where is it implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי יוחנן's פסוק shows the number ten.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the number ten comes from in ״ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל״.

steps.title: First link: 'among' connects to קרח's group
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא links the word ״תוך״ in ״ונקדשתי״ to ״הבדלו מתוך העדה״, which was said about קרח's group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: We learn from the word 'among' that appears in two places. Here it says, 'And I will be made holy among the children of Israel.' And there it says, 'Separate yourselves from among this congregation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer with a גזירה שוה, which links two פסוקים that share a word. This is the first step of a two-step chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both פסוקים use ״תוך״, ״ונקדשתי״ takes on the meaning of the עדה in קרח's story. So the holiness must happen in front of an עדה. But we still don't know how many people an עדה is, so a second link is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning from a word that appears in two פסוקים
'It comes from תוך and תוך', a link through the shared word
'Separate from among the congregation', said about קרח (במדבר ט"ז:כ"א)
'Here' and 'there', the two פסוקים being compared

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiya taught:
It is derived from "among" (and) "among,"
it is written here: "And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel,"
and it is written there: "Separate yourselves from among the congregation,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 12 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״תוך״ links ״ונקדשתי״ to the עדה of קרח.

steps.title: Second link: 'congregation' connects to the ten spies
steps.stepSummary: The word ״עדה״ links קרח's group to the bad מרגלים, who were ten. So an עדה is ten, and holiness needs ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learn from the word 'congregation' that appears in two places. There it says, 'How long will this evil congregation go on?' Just as there it means ten, here too it means ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the chain. A second גזירה שוה shows that an עדה is ten people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'evil congregation' refers to the מרגלים who spoke badly about ארץ ישראל. That was twelve spies minus יהושע and כלב, which is ten. So עדה means ten. By the chain, ״ונקדשתי״ needs ten, and so does every דבר שבקדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: A congregation, which here is shown to mean ten men
'How long for this evil congregation', said about the מרגלים (במדבר י"ד:כ"ז)
'Just as there, so too here', which carries the rule across

steps.whatToRemember: The chain works like this: ״ונקדשתי בתוך״ links by ״תוך״ to ״מתוך העדה״ (קרח). That links by ״עדה״ to ״לעדה הרעה״ (the מרגלים), who were ten. So every דבר שבקדושה needs ten.
steps.confusionAlert: There were twelve מרגלים, but the 'evil congregation' is only ten, because יהושע and כלב are not counted.

phrases.english: And it is derived from "congregation" (and) "congregation,"
as it is written there:
"How long (shall I bear) with this evil congregation" —
just as there (it means) ten,
so too here (it means) ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the two-step chain by giving the number ten.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עדה means ten, based on the bad מרגלים. So ״ונקדשתי״ needs ten.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any דבר שבקדושה needs a מנין of ten, learned through the chain תוך to עדה.

steps.title: Standing and sitting at a funeral needs ten out of respect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that מעמד ומושב needs ten. It explains that the leader calls out a formal, honorable announcement, and that style does not fit a group smaller than ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: we do not do the standing and sitting at a funeral with fewer than ten. Why not? Because the leader has to say 'Stand, dear friends, stand; sit, dear friends, sit.' Saying that to fewer than ten people is not proper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the funeral ceremony of standing and sitting. It explains why ten are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier items, this is not a דבר שבקדושה, so the פסוק of ״ונקדשתי״ does not apply. The reason here is respect: a grand announcement like 'dear friends, stand' only fits a real crowd of ten. Fewer than ten is called לאו אורח ארעא, meaning not proper conduct.

keyTerms.meaning: The funeral practice of standing up and sitting down several times on the way back from burial
Dear or honored ones
Less than (Aramaic)
Not proper conduct; not respectful

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume every item on this list needs ten because of קדושה. This one needs ten only because of respect.

phrases.english: And one does not perform the standing and sitting
with fewer than ten.
Since he needs to say:
"Stand, dear ones, stand;
sit, dear ones, sit"
with fewer than ten, it is not proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list, now that the source for דברים שבקדושה is finished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעמד ומושב needs ten because the formal announcement is not respectful with fewer.

steps.title: What is the mourners' blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about ברכת אבלים and ברכת חתנים, then asks which blessing ברכת אבלים refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: we do not say the mourners' blessing or the grooms' blessing with fewer than ten. The גמרא asks: what is this mourners' blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks what the term ברכת אבלים means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows the grooms' blessing, the שבע ברכות. The mourners' blessing is less familiar, so the גמרא first defines which ceremony the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing said for mourners
The blessings for a groom (שבע ברכות)
What is it?

phrases.english: And one does not say the mourners' blessing
and the grooms' blessing, etc.
What is the mourners' blessing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next item in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which blessing the term ברכת אבלים refers to

steps.title: It is the blessing said in the square
steps.stepSummary: The mourners' blessing is ברכת רחבה, the blessing said to comfort the mourners in the open square near the cemetery after the burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the blessing said in the square.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ברכת אבלים is the blessing given to the mourners in the square after the burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the burial, the people gathered in an open square near the cemetery and blessed the mourners that God should comfort them. That public ceremony is what needs ten.

keyTerms.meaning: An open square, here the place near the cemetery where people gathered after a burial

phrases.english: The blessing of the square.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ברכת אבלים is the blessing said in the square after the burial

steps.title: Mourners do not count toward the ten, but grooms do
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק in the name of רבי יוחנן rules that both blessings need ten. The mourners are not counted in the ten, but the grooms are.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the mourners' blessing needs ten, and the mourners themselves are not counted. The grooms' blessing needs ten, and the grooms are counted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יוחנן that backs up the answer and adds a detail: who counts toward the ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the mourners' blessing you need ten people besides the mourners, since the mourners are the ones receiving the comfort. For the grooms' blessing the groom himself counts, so nine others are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: With ten men
Part of the count; counted toward the quorum

steps.confusionAlert: Mourners and grooms are treated in opposite ways. Mourners do NOT count toward the ten. Grooms DO count.
steps.whatToRemember: ברכת אבלים needs ten not including the mourners. ברכת חתנים needs ten including the groom.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for how many people must be present at a comforting ceremony and at שבע ברכות.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The mourners' blessing is with ten,
and the mourners are not part of the count.
The grooms' blessing is with ten,
and the grooms are part of the count.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 17 and adds a counting rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten are needed for both blessings. Mourners are not counted, grooms are counted.

steps.title: זימון with God's name needs ten out of respect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that זימון with God's name needs ten. The reason is that you say 'Let us bless our God,' and it is not respectful to say this with fewer than ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: we do not do זימון after a meal with God's name with fewer than ten. Why not? Because he needs to say 'Let us bless our God,' and with fewer than ten that is not proper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the זימון with God's name, and explains why ten are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like מעמד ומושב, the reason is respect, not a פסוק. Mentioning God's name in the invitation ״נברך לאלהינו״ is fitting only before a group of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Inviting others to join in ברכת המזון (זימון)
With God's name
"Let us bless our God", the זימון wording used with ten

phrases.english: And one does not invite others to bless over food
with God's name, with fewer than ten, etc.
Since he needs to say
"Let us bless our God"
with fewer than ten, it is not proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reasoning as step 15 (לאו אורח ארעא) for a new item
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זימון with God's name needs ten because it is not respectful with fewer.

steps.title: Where do we learn that land is valued by nine and a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that consecrated land is valued by nine people and a כהן, and a person's value the same way. It then asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: land is valued by nine and a כהן, and a person the same way. The גמרא asks: where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last item and asks for its source. This sets up a derivation from פסוקים in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone consecrates a field and wants to redeem it, it must be valued, and the משנה says this takes ten people, one of whom is a כהן. This is neither a דבר שבקדושה nor a matter of respect, so the גמרא needs a specific source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lands; here, consecrated fields being valued for redemption
Priest; one of the ten must be a כהן
Similar to them; treated the same way
From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: And lands are valued by nine and a priest,
and a person is similar to them, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the final item in the משנה and opens a new search for a source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תורה source for valuing consecrated land and a person with nine and a כהן

steps.title: שמואל counts ten mentions of כהן to get nine ישראלים and one כהן
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the word כהן appears ten times in the פרשה. One mention requires a כהן, one excludes non-כהנים, and the remaining mentions are a מיעוט אחר מיעוט, which comes to include. The result is nine ישראלים and one כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The word כהן is written ten times in the פרשה. One is for itself, one is to exclude, and the rest are a limitation after a limitation, and a limitation after a limitation only comes to include. So it is nine ישראלים and one כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20, 'Where do we learn ten valuers, one of them a כהן?' שמואל finds the source in how many times the word כהן is written in the Torah section about valuing consecrated things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten mentions of כהן give us ten people. The first mention teaches that a כהן must be there, and the second teaches that only a כהן may do it. The extra mentions pile one limit on top of another, and by the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט that pile-up actually widens the rule, letting the other nine be ordinary ישראלים.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah section; here ויקרא chapter 27, about ערכין and consecrated things
For itself, meaning the word teaches its plain meaning
To exclude, to narrow the rule
A limitation after a limitation

keyTerms.term: אֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת
keyTerms.meaning: A double limitation only comes to include (to widen)

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but in this rule two limits in a row widen the law instead of narrowing it more. That is why extra mentions of כהן let non-כהנים join the panel.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
'Kohen' is written ten times in the section.
One is for itself (a Kohen is required),
(and one is to exclude non-Kohanim,)
and the rest are a limitation after a limitation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.english: and a limitation after a limitation only comes to include.
So: nine Israelites and one Kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: עֲשָׂרָה כֹּהֲנִים כְּתוּבִים בַּפָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ten mentions of כהן, read through the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, give ten valuers: nine ישראלים and one כהן.

steps.title: Why not five כהנים and five ישראלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's math. If the mentions keep switching between limiting and including, the split should be five כהנים and five ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: five כהנים and five ישראלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's reading. It suggests the mentions could take turns, so that one requires a כהן, the next allows a non-כהן, and so on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each double limit only widens the rule for the next mention, the mentions would alternate between כהן and non-כהן. That would give an even five-and-five split, not nine and one. The challenge asks why שמואל lets all the extra mentions widen together.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (introduces a competing reading)

phrases.english: But say instead:
five Kohanim and five Israelites!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's derivation
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's conclusion of nine ישראלים and one כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying מיעוט אחר מיעוט one mention at a time would make the mentions alternate, giving five כהנים and five ישראלים.

steps.title: The difficulty stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the challenge has no answer and leaves it as a קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the exchange by saying it has no answer to the five-and-five challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself, nine ישראלים and one כהן, stays in the משנה. Only שמואל's way of deriving it from the verses is left weak. 'קשיא' means the question is strong, not that the halacha is overturned.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stands unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here does not cancel the halacha of ten valuers with one כהן. It only says this particular derivation has an unsolved problem.
steps.whatToRemember: The ten-valuer rule stands, but שמואל's derivation from the ten mentions of כהן ends with an unanswered קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 22 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge to שמואל's derivation stays unanswered, but the משנה's rule is not overturned.

steps.title: How can a person be holy enough to need valuing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a person is valued the same way, then asks how a person can become קדוש at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a person is like them.' Can a person become holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה. It asks what it means to value a person like consecrated property, since a human being cannot be dedicated to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Valuing makes sense for land that was made קדוש and now needs to be redeemed. A person, though, cannot become Temple property. So the גמרא needs to find what case the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Like them; treated the same way
Consecrated, holy (belonging to the Temple)

phrases.english: 'And a person is like them.'
Can a person become holy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָדָם כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן. אָדָם מִי קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second clause of the משנה quoted in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of 'valuing a person' the משנה means, since a person cannot be consecrated

steps.title: רבי אבהו: it is someone who pledges his own value
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the משנה means a person who says 'דמי עלי,' pledging to give the Temple money equal to his own worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is one who says, 'My value is upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question by explaining the case. The person himself is not holy; he has promised to give his money value to the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about the person becomes holy. The pledge creates a debt of money, and to know how much he owes, someone has to figure out what he is worth. That figuring is the 'valuing' the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: 'My value is upon me': a pledge to give the Temple one's market worth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'דמי עלי' (my market value, which must be assessed) with 'ערכי עלי' (a fixed amount set by the Torah by age and gender, so no assessment is needed).

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
It is one who says, 'My value is upon me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בְּאוֹמֵר דְּמֵי עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is one who pledges his own monetary value ('דמי עלי'), which then has to be assessed.

steps.title: A ברייתא: such a person is valued like a slave
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי אבהו: someone who says 'דמי עלי' is assessed as if he were an עבד being sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: One who says 'My value is upon me' is assessed like a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבי אבהו and to show how such a person's value is figured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that 'דמי עלי' leads to a real money assessment. The measuring method is to ask what he would sell for as an עבד. This sets up the next move, which links עבד to land.

keyTerms.meaning: They assess him; they estimate his value
A slave

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One who says, 'My value is upon me' —
they assess him as a slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's case and gives the method of assessment
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's case of 'דמי עלי' and how it is valued
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: one who says 'דמי עלי' is assessed as an עבד

steps.title: A slave is compared to land, so ten valuers apply
steps.stepSummary: An עבד is compared to land by a פסוק. So the same ten-valuer rule used for consecrated land applies to valuing a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a slave is compared to land, as it is written: 'And you shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit as a possession.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the chain by linking עבד to land through a פסוק. This explains why a person is valued 'like them,' with nine ישראלים and one כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain runs: the person is valued like an עבד, and an עבד is compared to land. The פסוק calls עבדים an inherited 'אחוזה' (holding), the same word used for land. So whatever rule applies to valuing land also applies to valuing a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Is compared (by a היקש, a link made in the Torah's wording)
Land, real estate
A permanent holding, a word used for land

steps.whatToRemember: A person who says 'דמי עלי' is valued like an עבד, and an עבד is compared to land. So valuing a person also takes ten people, one of them a כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש between עבדים and land comes up across ש״ס for other laws too, such as how עבדים are acquired and how claims about them work.

phrases.english: And a slave is compared to land,
as it is written:
'And you shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you,'
'to inherit as a possession.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the link from the עבד assessment to the land rule
steps.raayaObject: That a person is valued with the same ten-person rule as land
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כה:מו, which calls עבדים an 'אחוזה' like land

steps.title: New משנה: at least three verses, and one verse at a time for the translator
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that each person who reads from the Torah must read at least three פסוקים. When there is a מתורגמן, the reader may not read him more than one פסוק at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who reads from the תורה should not read fewer than three פסוקים. He should not read more than one פסוק at a time to the מתורגמן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It gives two practical rules for reading the Torah in public: a minimum length for each reader, and a limit on how much is read to the מתורגמן at one time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule sets a minimum: a reading shorter than three פסוקים does not count as a proper portion. The second rule protects the translation. In those days a מתורגמן translated the reading aloud into Aramaic. If the reader gave him more than one פסוק at a time, the מתורגמן could get mixed up and translate wrongly.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה.' It marks the start of a new משנה.
The person reading from the Torah scroll in shul
He should not do less than (a minimum amount)
Verses of the Torah
The translator who said the reading aloud in Aramaic for the listeners

steps.confusionAlert: The three-פסוקים minimum applies to EACH person called up to read. It is not the total for the whole reading. Also, the 'one verse' limit is about how much the reader says before pausing for the מתורגמן. It is not about how much he reads overall.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that each עולה reads at least three פסוקים is still followed today in every public Torah reading.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: One who reads from the Torah
phrases.notes: Refers to public reading in shul

phrases.english: should not read fewer than three verses,
and he should not read to the translator
phrases.notes: The reader pauses so the מתורגמן can translate aloud

phrases.english: more than one verse (at a time).
phrases.notes: This keeps the מתורגמן from getting confused

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַקּוֹרֵא בְּתוֹרָה לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה פְּסוּקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic. It is not connected to the previous discussion of valuations and consecrated land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each Torah reader reads at least three פסוקים. When there is a מתורגמן, the reader gives him only one פסוק at a time.
